data.statement: The Rupi checkpoint adapter is read-only: it converts accepted primitive results into deterministic lifecycle checkpoints and does not invoke mutation primitives.
The Distiller entrypoint validates v2 project identity fields and project paths and fails closed on unsupported or malformed project configuration.

The ordinary-repair tests verify missing, stale, or malformed projections can be rebuilt deterministically from valid history without touching history and invalid history requires exceptional recovery.
The copied-artifacts record classifies extracted content as either framework material or reference-corpus material and requires listed parity copies to remain byte-identical to their source blobs.
The accepted Phase 6 baseline records parity evidence commit fb7290622d6a9d929a059f111cdd60cd50496fcf as the consumer pin and marks Phase 6.0H PASS with Phase 6.1 unblocked.
The RGP fixture corpus includes a valid graph where empirical observations ground a derived claim through premise references.
The authority-grant runtime validates immutable grant-issuance evidence at apply time and supports revocation by the grantor or protected root.

The Rupi update/recovery tests verify updates use the same installer mutation primitive, recovery requires bounded recovery intent and replanning, managed drift stops mutation, and real project-owned authority state is preserved byte-for-byte.

The greenfield first-invocation workflow extends a fresh install/bootstrap with explicit evidence, activation-bundle preparation, a fixed provider-boundary candidate, immutable finalize/replay checks, and authority/canonical-boundary verification.
The R16-R18 completion record records G1 through G10 as passed.

The Reasoning Graph Protocol Engineer directive defines RGP as domain-independent and assigns generic protocol, validator, evaluation, pressure-case, and framework work without project-specific canonical authority.
The invocation-request schema requires an explicit project root, non-empty evidence and source registry, invocation identity/time, and output paths under reasoning-distiller-invocation/1.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract states that conversation itself grants no authority and creates no semantic operation unavailable through the accepted RIL boundary.
The project-identity bridge tests verify a v2 identity is valid bootstrap state and the first-admission base reuses that exact explicit project identity.

The pre-approval proposal-revalidation design contract requires complete apply-time validation independently after approval creation, so approval does not freeze project state or waive later validation.

The RGP output schema permits only observation, decision, assumption, uncertainty, and claim records; only supports, contradicts, depends_on, and supersedes relations; and requires primary provenance for non-derived observations.
The install/bootstrap Rupi handoff deliberately keeps protected authority setup outside its lifecycle surface.
The Rupi update/recovery tests verify failed updates roll back and Rupi never reports false success or performs surfaced authority setup.

The clean-source promotion workflow requires default-branch dispatch, mirrors development source into release-source while excluding the installed framework tree, verifies the clean result, and checks release-source has not moved before pushing.

The self-consumption isolation execution record reports PASS for installing and invoking an accepted release entirely from .reasoning-distiller/ while adjacent framework source roots were made unavailable.
The RIL mutation runtime implements proposal revalidation with explicit classifications and validates proposal and approval artifacts before state transitions.
The accepted install-package contract makes manifest content identity the semantic identity of installed package content and verifies the SHA-256 of exact archive transport bytes separately.
The Human-Agent tests verify cross-session resume reconstructs from durable references and protected ceremonies plus final control return remain explicit adapter boundaries.
The preserved reference transaction demonstrates provenance-preserving reuse and guarded update of an existing decision while adding source/source-observation and measured proposition records.
The Steward-authorization runtime validates both operator and role state before applying authorization changes.
The RIL activation-evidence workflow independently runs and compiles the R8 activation conformance suite.
The production-invocation tests verify installed runtime can operate without source-repository fallback and leaves project-owned authority and canonical bytes unchanged.
The bootstrap tests verify conflicting identity, missing installation, configuration/path conflicts, and symlink-managed paths fail without unauthorized repair or mutation.

The accepted installer-runner contract defines `rd_install.py` as a deterministic network-independent Python 3 CLI that consumes local package files, an expected transport digest, and an explicit project target while leaving package retrieval and release selection to the runner.

The installer recovery tests verify interrupted transactions restore or finalize according to journal phase, recovery is idempotent, and orphan backups or malformed journals fail closed without touching project-owned files.
The operator-management contract permits authority-grant-derived approval only for exact non-root `operator-registry.disable` proposals; protected-root transfer remains explicitly non-delegable.

The Rupi R1 implementation conformance record reports R1 through R8 complete on implementation baseline `ebc2a6bebfc76790d4fa192c6e7e980428d05d6c`, including adversarial proof that Rupi has no alternate installer, updater, bootstrapper, authority system, recovery system, reconciliation path, admission path, or Canon mutation path.
The docs-release-policy shadow review records four useful durable propositions with zero review defects and states that the candidate preserved the narrowed docs-only exception without widening it.

The package-build configuration allowlists admission, agents, backends, protocols, runtime, schemas, and validators as managed release roots while excluding CI, docs, evaluation, project knowledge, and tests from the installed package.
The evaluation corpus preserves the exact Phase-1 input cases separately from current project state so repeated Distiller runs can be compared against a stable reference set.
The Distiller entrypoint accepts only repository_file and governed_artifact ingestion source types and rejects selecting the same locator under both source types.

The P8 release baseline defines accepted immutable release publication as a package, manifest, transport digest, installer, package validator, and schemas tied to an exact source commit and content identity.
The accepted installer-runner contract requires failed validation to preserve or restore the previous known installation.
The bootstrap tests verify minimum project state creation is idempotent, explicit identity creates project/2, and a known v1 configuration can migrate only with explicit identity.
The reconciliation tests verify conflicting second dispositions fail closed and candidate byte mutation creates a new identity rather than rewriting an existing disposition.
The bootstrap runtime permits an exact v1 project configuration to remain unchanged or to migrate to v2 only when an explicit complete v2 identity is supplied.

The RIL orchestrator design contract states that bootstrap creates no operator authority and that the first authority-sensitive operation without an operator requires an explicit initial-operator setup ceremony.
The release-source guard workflow refuses a release-source branch that contains installed .reasoning-distiller state.

The operator-registry contract makes operator events authoritative and the current operator file a deterministic projection, and initial-root establishment creates administrative operator identity without granting semantic-reconciliation or admission authority.
The governance runtime represents operational provenance as a content-addressed reasoning-distiller-provenance/1 artifact and provides typed-reference parsing and dispatch.

The distillation-ingestion operation constructs an invocation request and activation bundle without calling a model or mutating canonical knowledge, and excludes `.git/`, `.reasoning-distiller/`, and `project-knowledge/` from evidence selection.
The RGP fixture test runner validates the preserved valid and invalid fixture corpus against the current RGP validator rather than relying only on schema parsing.
The Phase 0 baseline requires raw candidate preservation plus separate evaluation diagnostics and prohibits mixing scoring diagnostics into the durable candidate graph.
The RIL common-mutation workflow independently runs and compiles the R1-R3 mutation substrate conformance suite.
The accepted workflow contract binds a durable workflow to one immutable authenticated bounded intent.
The grant-operations runtime maps grant authority into bounded role-registry and operator-disable approval/application paths rather than a generic unrestricted mutation path.
The Distiller core derives a candidate submission ID deterministically from the invocation identifier and canonical candidate graph bytes.

The release-package builder validates the source tree, collects only configured managed files, constructs a canonical manifest/content identity, builds deterministic tar.gz bytes, and verifies the resulting archive.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract does not permit an authority grant to waive or consume a required materiality acknowledgement.

The Steward-authorization contract defines `semantic_reconciliation` and `admission` as independent scopes, makes authorization events authoritative with a derived current projection, and states that registration alone never grants a Steward scope.
The project bootstrap runtime recognizes both the exact legacy reasoning-distiller-project/1 configuration and the reasoning-distiller-project/2 identity contract.
The RGP fixture corpus includes an invalid observation with an empty provenance object.
The consumer-migration record states that migration must preserve project-owned knowledge and authority while replacing cross-repository runtime coupling with the project-local installed framework.
The Steward-authorization runtime maintains a separate steward_authorization domain with its own proposals, approvals, events, projection rebuilding, and read path.
The operator-management tests verify root transfer requires current-root approval, exact confirmation, an active target with all core capabilities, and preserves exactly one root after success.
The accepted workflow contract states that workflow intent itself grants no downstream approval, activation, semantic authority, admission authority, or resource lock.
The common mutation substrate preserves a distinction between direct-operator approval and authority-grant-derived approval while binding both approval forms to exactly one immutable proposal.

The release-acceptance workflow checks out an exact release-source commit, rebuilds the package twice, validates production payload, creates or verifies an immutable GitHub release, and persists PASS evidence only after guarding the main-branch base.

The RIL orchestrator design contract states that RGP, PEMS, and COVE are package-owned normative contracts and consuming projects may not fork, replace, supersede, or reinterpret those protocol contracts.
The RIL role-registry workflow independently runs and compiles the R6 role-registry conformance suite.

The streaming-performance-baseline shadow review records zero review defects and notes that the candidate preserved measured latency, health metrics, bounded inference, a loading-before-LOD decision, and unresolved latency composition without universalizing the result.
The Rupi lifecycle adapter composes installer, bootstrap, status, and recovery primitives and states that it owns no installer, lifecycle, authority, or intent semantics.
The PEMS/RGP compatibility fixture set distinguishes lossless exportable domain records from states that cannot be represented losslessly in RGP/1.
The install-package contract tests verify content identity is independent of file ordering and transport digest metadata but changes when semantic package fields change.
The Distiller directive treats source identifiers as opaque, prohibits inferring source authority from identifier spelling, and prefers omission over invented provenance or semantic repair.

The storage-verification tests verify valid admitted state is verified read-only and deterministic, while missing/incomplete canonical pairs, noncanonical PEMS bytes, schema-invalid PEMS, COVE mismatch, receipt mismatch, and symlink canonical files fail.

The package validator computes content identity from semantic manifest content, validates safe relative paths and managed-root containment, and separately validates package manifests and installation records against schemas.

The Steward handoff trial specification requires an explicitly project-authorized Steward for reconciliation and forbids treating repository presence, role names, CI execution, or the specification itself as an authority grant.
The RIL orchestrator runtime routes bounded operation requests to existing primitives and returns normalized orchestration results rather than implementing independent semantic mutation logic.

The role-registry contract states that registry membership grants no Steward, reconciliation, admission, protocol-governance, or invocation authority and that the package-provided `steward:default` role is immutable, always available, and never authorized merely by registration.
The legacy distillation validator provides deterministic structural validation of Reasoning Distiller graph output using the same closed record/relation and provenance concepts.
The grant-operation tests verify grant creation requires operation-specific grantor capability and apply-time logic validates immutable grant issuance evidence.
The package-builder workflow enforces clean release source, runs builder pressure tests, builds twice from identical inputs, validates the generated manifest, and audits top-level package roots.

The orchestrator tests verify read-only routing preserves primitive results, unknown actions call no primitive, arguments are forwarded exactly, plan/approve/apply remain separate routes, reconciliation authority evidence is forwarded unchanged, and admit does not implicitly run storage verification.
The protected-confirmation runtime binds exact confirmations only for a fixed set of protected confirmation classes rather than accepting arbitrary confirmation labels.

The install-package final plan records the accepted distribution model as an immutable versioned local package retrieved by an authorized runner and installed with deterministic `rd_install.py`, rather than cross-repository runtime coupling.

The Rupi lifecycle-agent design contract keeps installer mutation, project bootstrap, operator or Steward authority setup, and semantic or admission work as distinct primitive boundaries; Rupi must reuse the accepted installer for update and may not use the legacy Steward setup utility as an alternate authority path.
The RIL admission workflow independently runs and compiles the R13 admission conformance suite.
The reference-proof copy manifest preserves one exact Steward v2 admission transaction and its exact deterministic proof summary as reference-corpus parity evidence.
The accepted install-package contract states that compatibility metadata declares what the package can work with but does not grant authority or select an active backend for a project.
The current release-source guard fails when an installed .reasoning-distiller/ tree exists or is tracked on release-source.
The Distiller core validates that every provenance source referenced by a model candidate exists in the supplied source registry before submission.

The exceptional-recovery contract requires the protected root, preserves damaged authoritative history byte-for-byte, binds approval to the exact damaged-history fingerprint and continuation state, and stores recovery separately as append-only evidence.

The RIL activation-evidence contract validates one exact runtime invocation, registered role, requested Steward scope, current role availability, and current Steward assignment; authorization or role-name matching alone is insufficient.
The activation runtime loads current role and Steward-authorization state and validates activation against those durable states rather than treating activation evidence alone as authority.

The storage-verification contract defines R14 as a read-only check of canonical PEMS schema/integrity, deterministic PEMS bytes, exact COVE encoding and round-trip, and a matching immutable admission receipt.

The common-no-clip-camera shadow review records validator PASS, low review burden, zero invented propositions, zero material omissions, zero provenance/classification/authority issues, and no canonical modification or admission request.
The exceptional-recovery runtime has separate plan, approval, apply, recovery-record, and recovered-domain replay primitives.

The Steward handoff trial specification requires candidate integrity and admission separation, with successful reconciliation ending in a durable Steward disposition and no implied canonical mutation.

The PEMS admission fixture set includes cases for canonical identity reuse, distinct identity under domain refinement, atomic derived-subgraph admission, and other reconciliation/admission pressure conditions.
The initial-operator tests verify second distinct roots and conflicting projections are rejected and that initial-operator setup creates no Steward or canonical state.
The greenfield consumer record closes GFCT-001 and identifies explicit evidence plus first invocation construction as the next independent boundary after bootstrap.
The admission tests verify exact retry is no-change while candidate mutation after reconciliation, stale plans, record collisions, and conflicting second admission fail closed.
The accepted CLI and Human-to-Agent contracts require proposal-applicability revalidation immediately before a fresh direct approval is created.
The installation guide requires selecting and retrieving one exact accepted release before running the local installer and warns against installing from an unpinned branch such as main.

The cross-adapter tests verify Human-Agent and CLI surfaces preserve identical proposal, approval, D3, workflow, grant, event, continuation, and delegable-apply artifacts/results when routing the same operations.

The Rupi checkpoint tests verify checkpoint construction is deterministic and non-mutating, completion requires primitive PASS, blockers/next actions are preserved, no percentage-progress field exists, and malformed primitive observations fail closed.

The Rupi R6 primitive amendment wraps the legacy installer recovery primitive through shared orchestration without reimplementing recovery semantics and requires recovery to be followed by fresh transition planning before continuation.

The install-package manifest schema binds version, source commit, content identity, transport SHA-256, compatibility, managed roots, and exact file entries under reasoning-distiller-install-package/1.

The exceptional-recovery tests verify valid history cannot be recovered, recovery is protected-root and evidence-backed, changed damage after approval fails closed, and later damage mutation is detected by recovery records.

The live-model activation specification treats hosted model execution as an external provider boundary, requires the exact supplied evidence and registry to be used, preserves invalid raw model output rather than repairing it, and stops after immutable candidate production.

The install-package final plan defines update as installation of another verified package through the same installer transaction, removing old files only when the prior verified manifest proves package ownership and leaving unmanaged files untouched.
The ordinary operator-management path validates managers and ordinary proposals separately from root-transfer preconditions and confirmation logic.
The Distiller core states and implements no model execution, admission, canonical mutation, or source-repository fallback.

The install-package final plan defines a failure/recovery pressure suite covering bad transport, manifest mismatch, traversal or duplicate paths, incompatible project/backend state, managed drift, interrupted activation or restore, same-version different-content identity, missing runtime files, and source-repository unavailability.

The repository README states that the Distiller produces candidates, the project Steward owns semantic reconciliation and admission authority, and deterministic execution applies only an already-authorized reconciliation plan.
The installation guide requires package SHA-256 verification before installation and directs users to review the repository diff after installation.
The automation-boundary tests verify materiality cannot be bypassed by an in-scope grant and is revalidated before grant consumption.

The install-package contract tests reject duplicate/casefold-colliding/unsafe paths, files outside managed roots, generated installation metadata in release payloads, invalid modes/digests, and incorrect content identity.

The scoring rubric defines fabricated provenance, invented project decisions, unsupported bug causality, hidden-reasoning reconstruction, and unsupported causal relations as hard failures regardless of numeric score.
The RIL ordinary-repair workflow independently runs and compiles the R10 projection-repair conformance suite.
The RGP fixture corpus includes an invalid case proving that a present premise array cannot be empty.

The governed-ingestion operation requires governed evidence to be explicitly selected and states that source authority must not be inferred from filenames, directories, headings, source identifiers, or prose.

The automation-boundary tests verify stale state, exhausted or revoked grants, unresolved activation/conditions, grant ambiguity, wildcard inference, scope expansion, and protected operations all stop automation fail closed.
The accepted installer-runner contract places package retrieval and release selection outside installer execution.

The accepted install-package contract places generic framework-managed state under .reasoning-distiller/ while keeping project knowledge, authority, policy, activation, evidence, canonical state, and integration material outside that managed root.
The accepted installer-runner contract requires managed-file drift to fail closed by default.
The P7 update-proof record demonstrates a second package-version update through the same installer mechanism with an auditable managed-tree diff rather than a separate updater implementation.
The general RIL Test Suite runs the complete Python unit-test discovery suite on pushes to main and pull requests.
The RIL exceptional-recovery workflow independently runs and compiles the R11 recovery conformance suite.

The project-identity amendment requires first admission to construct a project-seeded PEMS/2 base from valid project/2 identity and requires admission to fail with PROJECT_IDENTITY_REQUIRED when neither valid v2 project identity nor existing canonical PEMS is available.
The admission runtime fails with BASE_MISMATCH when an admission plan was not built against the current canonical PEMS bytes.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract places delegated authority in the grant rather than in the agent.
The bootstrap tests verify project bootstrap creates no authority or canonical state.
The accepted installer-runner contract defines rd_install.py as the deterministic Python 3 installer CLI.

The accepted installer-runner contract excludes current network state, mutable repository heads, implicit version discovery, environment-specific source paths, and current time from the inputs allowed to determine installed framework content.
The workflow runtime stores an immutable workflow definition, append-only workflow events, explicit history/normative heads, and a replay-derived workflow projection.
The authority-grant runtime revalidates a proposal before grant-derived approval issuance and refuses issuance when the proposal is not classified APPLICABLE.

The reconciliation tests verify activation authority is required, candidates must come from submissions, successful reconciliation persists immutable disposition and activation evidence, and no admission/canonical state is created.

The preserved reference admission transaction uses rgp-pems2-admission-transaction/2 with an exact expected base digest, explicit reuse records, one guarded record update, four new records, and no new relations.
The Distiller core explicitly excludes .git, .reasoning-distiller, and project-knowledge roots from evidence expansion.
The workflow runtime distinguishes core normative events from namespaced extension events and prevents semantic event appends after terminal workflow state.

The status tests verify lifecycle blockers have precedence, missing projections are classified rebuildable without mutation, authorization scopes remain independent, evidence/candidate presence never asserts semantic validity, and status is strictly read-only.

The RIL activation-evidence primitive is read-only, persists no activation state, grants no authority, and requires downstream authority-bearing primitives to receive or bind the exact activation artifact or digest they validated.
The RGP uncertainty-import fixtures map RGP/1 uncertainty to current PEMS unresolved_item records with open resolution state rather than silently converting uncertainty into a proposition claim.
The package-contract workflow validates package examples and canonical installer entrypoint, then runs package-contract and deterministic installer-runner tests.
The activation runtime constructs and validates reasoning-distiller-role-activation/1 artifacts that bind a role to an invocation identifier and explicit activation source.
The accepted install-package contract defines package semantic identity as the manifest content identity.
The accepted install-package contract verifies the transport SHA-256 of exact archive bytes separately from package semantic content identity.
The Steward directive explicitly states that the generic role contract does not grant authority by itself.
The resource-loading-roadmap shadow review records zero review defects and notes that the candidate preserved the roadmap decision while keeping the unisolated loading cause explicitly uncertain.

The pre-approval proposal-revalidation design contract states that an APPLICABLE result grants no authority, that revalidation cannot rewrite the immutable proposal, and that STALE, BLOCKED, or INVALID results prohibit fresh approval creation.

The Rupi lifecycle-agent design contract requires Rupi to reconstruct lifecycle truth from accepted status and durable project state, prohibits a private authoritative progress database, and requires handoff instead of silently continuing into semantic processing when setup makes it possible.
The RIL orchestrator workflow independently tests composition-only R15 behavior and compiles the orchestrator primitive.
The consumer-migration document requires consumers to pin the framework by immutable commit SHA and keeps project knowledge packages and active canonical state owned by the consuming project.
The R16-R18 completion record identifies main commit d1573f326a62f81ce725b62e13824d6d31f81aaf as the stable verified implementation baseline for R16-R18 conformance.
The PEMS/2 validator performs deterministic structural, compatibility, migration, admission-pressure, graph-integrity, and candidate-document checks without mutating canonical memory.

The bounded-chunk-loading shadow review records five useful durable propositions, zero omissions/inventions/false relations/provenance or authority issues, low review burden, and no canonical modification or admission request.

The Phase 6 consumer-migration record reports PASS for the voxel-engine migration, including project-owned canonical state and authority rules, a pinned framework executor, retirement of embedded generic executable/schema implementation, and zero active workflow references to the embedded framework.

The common mutation substrate defines proposals as immutable intent with no mutation, approvals as exact-proposal-bound authority evidence, append-only mutation events as authoritative state, and projections as derived replay products.

The orchestrator-composition contract makes R15 composition-only: it must delegate to existing primitives, must not synthesize authority-sensitive inputs, and must preserve delegated primitive results without reinterpretation.

The package-builder tests verify content changes alter content and transport identities, source-commit changes alter semantic package identity without changing the file set, and generated Python cache files do not affect the package.
The Distiller core reads only the evidence listed in the request and constructs activation bundles containing the local directive, fixed evidence, source registry, and optional source context.

The Distiller ingestion tests verify reserved roots are excluded, symlink evidence is rejected, missing project configuration fails closed, and differing existing ingestion artifacts are never overwritten.
The repository README describes Reasoning Distiller as a standalone knowledge-system framework extracted from loteque/gdscript-voxel-engine under a Phase 6.0 extraction plan.

The production invocation contract fixes the evidence set before model activation and prohibits the Distiller from autonomously searching for additional project facts or inferring authority from source identifiers or locators.
The operation-delegability classification fails closed as non-delegable unless an operation has an explicit accepted DELEGABLE declaration.
The RIL architecture synthesis states that ordinary repair may deterministically rebuild derived projections but may not alter authoritative history.
The project-identity amendment retains exact v1 bootstrap configuration as a compatibility state and permits v1-to-v2 migration only when all v2 identity fields are explicitly supplied.

The common mutation substrate requires grant applicability, scope, availability, consumption accounting, approval creation, and the grant approval-issued event to be atomic with respect to grant normative state; stale races fail rather than rebase.

The installer tests verify managed drift, unexpected managed files, bad transport digest, incompatible project contracts, unknown managed roots, and post-activation validation failure all fail closed with project files preserved or the previous install restored.

The PEMS/2 schema requires semantic, project_id, records, and relations and describes graph integrity, identity admission, provenance semantics, deterministic normalization, and retention as semantic validation responsibilities beyond JSON Schema.

The Extraction Parity workflow runs RGP fixture parity, Project Knowledge Package checks, framework isolation, frozen blob integrity, PEMS/2 and uncertainty-import checks, guarded admission pressure tests, preserved candidate checks, and frozen Steward proof verification in one parity job.
The RIL storage-verification workflow independently runs and compiles the R14 storage verification conformance suite.

The Phase 0 baseline defines five materially different real-project reasoning cases covering authority ownership, offline/runtime separation, governed validation requirements, bounded investigation, and unresolved deployed-runtime failure.
The Phase-1 closeout marks phase1_stable true with no blocking reasons and explicitly retains human review/admission controls rather than authorizing automatic canonical admission.
The admission tests verify that admission requires independent admission authority and that a reconciliation recommendation alone is not admission authority.

The accepted-release greenfield retest reports PASS after installed rd_bootstrap.py created exactly the minimum project-owned project-knowledge structure, returned ALREADY_BOOTSTRAPPED on replay, and created no canonical or authority state.
The RIL operator-management workflow independently runs and compiles the R5 operator-management conformance suite.

The ordinary-repair contract permits deterministic replacement or recreation of derived projections only after authoritative replay succeeds; invalid event history stops with exceptional-recovery-required and no mutation.
The Steward-authorization contract requires an authorized human operator to approve an exact Steward-scope proposal and states that the approving operator does not thereby become a Steward.
The Rupi primitive map defines a closed consequential action vocabulary whose entries map each Rupi action to one accepted status, install, bootstrap, authority, repair, or human-agent primitive.
The Phase 6 reference-proof workflow copies an exact proof fixture from the frozen source, verifies source/destination blob identities, writes a manifest, and commits the copied artifacts.

The bounded-authority-grant design contract requires materiality pauses, immediately-before proposal revalidation, and independent apply-time primitive validation to remain effective for grant-derived approvals.
The Phase 6 decouple workflow replaces provenance-only backend schema location and explicitly rejects hidden consuming-project coupling before committing the decoupled framework locator.
The production-invocation tests verify invalid RGP is preserved but not submitted and that missing evidence, digest mismatch, output collision, and unregistered provenance fail closed.

The frozen extraction baseline identifies loteque/gdscript-voxel-engine commit 1c25bf7cc858218941476097a3a5ac5ba204f270 as the source snapshot and records rgp/1 semantics as frozen with no semantic change authorized.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract defines an authority grant as prospective bounded human authority.
The RIL reconciliation workflow independently runs and compiles the R12 reconciliation conformance suite.

The Rupi authority-flow tests verify protected confirmation is exact but non-authoritative, operator and Steward targets are never inferred, each protected mutation requires its own ceremony, and authority setup creates no activation or semantic state.

The current release-status record reports PASS for Reasoning Distiller v0.5.2, source commit `90bc23ed90f12f06d41d019c79994747709ab326`, content identity `sha256:db4afb76e9cf1ae6abcc837a74bb26aa290528672bbfee5a9fa6839f48121c24`, and transport SHA-256 `e83814c2ff050fb63f609c1738e1d8ebdf1adbf196e32f2dd8d17796f7bb3ca3`.
The accepted Human-to-Agent and workflow contracts require a valid materiality pause to interrupt consequential continuation.

The role-registry tests verify default Steward role presence does not create authority, role planning is deterministic, scoped snapshots affect only roles within scope, and forbidden protocol/package roles or unknown rd capabilities are rejected.
The Phase-1 independent closeout records 15 validator-passing runs across five cases and three fresh invocations, with every recorded run scoring 18 of 18 and no hard failures.

The bootstrap runtime creates only the configured project-knowledge evidence, invocation, and submission directories plus project.json, and treats conflicting files, symlinks, or unsupported project configuration as failures.
The accepted CLI and Human-to-Agent contracts keep proposal creation, approval creation, and application as distinct operations.
The RIL CLI runtime discovers project state, inventories typed durable artifacts, renders workflow/grant/event views, and dispatches requested operations through the runtime primitives.

The bounded-authority-grant design contract records grant lifecycle and consumption through an append-only authority-grant event chain with exact expected-head concurrency, and states that revocation prevents future approval issuance without rewriting previously issued authority evidence.

The adversarial Rupi tests verify administrative language, repository/runner identity, install-only intent, readiness labels, legacy setup availability, and prior conversation cannot manufacture operator, Steward, reconciliation, or admission authority.
The authority-grant tests verify grant definitions are immutable, content-addressed, and idempotent and that non-delegable operations fail closed at grant creation.
The Phase-1 closeout records required propositions as present in 3 of 3 runs for all five cases and required uncertainty as present in 3 of 3 runs for the investigation and deployed-UI-failure cases.
The RGP Submission Protocol does not grant canonical admission, alter RGP semantics, select a canonical backend, or transfer ownership of project knowledge.

The installer is a deterministic network-independent local installer that verifies release identity, archive shape, managed drift, project compatibility, transition state, and installed-tree validity before/after mutation.

The project-identity amendment defines `reasoning-distiller-project/2` with explicit project-owned id, name, repository, and summary fields and prohibits the framework from inferring those identity fields from repository or environment state.
The Distiller entrypoint determines source type from the explicit ingestion selection and documents that deterministic source-ID spelling is bookkeeping rather than an authority source.

The project bootstrap contract defines bootstrap as a deterministic creator of minimum project-owned invocation/evidence/submission structure and explicitly excludes operator, Steward, canonical, admission, evidence-fact, and role authority creation.

The production-invocation workflow validates invocation schemas, verifies the reference adapter identity, runs the production invocation conformance suite, and proves the packaged payload contains the runtime adapter and invocation schemas.
The deterministic installer tests verify clean install/update changes only the managed tree, same inputs produce the same installed payload/metadata, and downgrades require explicit authorization.

The v1 admission executor applies a Steward-authorized admission plan only to an exact PEMS/2 snapshot and includes deterministic PEMS normalization, graph-integrity validation, and COVE encoding/round-trip logic.
The accepted workflow and Human-to-Agent contracts make auto-advance a continuation-eligibility mechanism rather than a source of authority for advanced operations.
The current Distiller entrypoint is a compatibility adapter over rd_distill_core.py that adds explicit governed_artifact source selection and reasoning-distiller-project/2 configuration support.

The Rupi primitive-inventory tests freeze the required action surface, require each action to name exactly one governing primitive, keep protected confirmation distinct, and reject legacy Steward setup as an authority route.

The install-package final plan requires installed runtime and already-retrieved installer execution to remain functional with the source repository unavailable and network access disabled, with no remote fallback for missing runtime files.
The storage-verification runtime performs read-only validation of canonical PEMS/COVE bytes, PEMS schema/integrity, deterministic COVE decoding, and immutable admission receipts.
The consumer-migration document prohibits hard-coded framework reads of project state and requires project paths and configuration to be supplied through project-owned package and workflow inputs.
The reconciliation runtime validates a supplied reconciliation assessment and immutable candidate, persists a reconciliation disposition, and operates under the semantic_reconciliation scope.
The authority-grant runtime requires explicit non-empty operation classes and explicit scope targets/constraints, and rejects unsupported or duplicate scope fields.
The operational-provenance design contract defines provenance as immutable content-addressed observational context bound to an exact subject, while keeping normative subject identity unchanged.
The role runtime validates the approving operator against operator state and separates role registration from Steward authorization state.

The production invocation contract makes request validation, evidence digest checks, activation-bundle construction, RGP validation, submission identity, persistence rules, and failure classification deterministic for fixed local inputs.

The RIL orchestrator design contract requires explicit project evidence, prohibits orchestration from silently broadening a Distiller evidence set, and requires unknown or conflicting authority-sensitive state to fail closed.
The authority-grant runtime stores immutable grant definitions plus append-only grant events and derives a grant projection by replay.

The shared-orchestration tests verify delegable operator and role proposals can auto-advance through a common path while stale D3, materiality pauses, ambiguous grants, and workflow scope failures stop before grant consumption.
The accepted install-package contract requires manifest paths to remain normalized, unique, relative, non-escaping package paths and excludes symlink package entries in v1.
The current release-status record identifies `reasoning-distiller-project/2` as the project contract and records `semantic_authority_changed` as false for v0.5.2.
The Steward-authorization tests verify scopes begin unassigned, the default Steward is not automatic, authorization scopes are independent, and reassignment/revocation affect only the selected scope.
The Distiller ingestion tests verify deterministic and idempotent request/bundle creation, stable source IDs/digests, recursive sorted directory expansion, and scriptable non-interactive invocation.

The Rupi install/bootstrap handoff tests verify the exact install→status→bootstrap→status chain stops at the authority boundary, bootstrap requires bounded intent, and failures never advance into authority work.

The composite-status contract defines status as a read-only projection over independently reportable lifecycle dimensions, applies explicit blocker precedence, and distinguishes REBUILDABLE projection state from corruption without repairing it.

The Project Knowledge Package schema defines project identity, compatible framework contracts, project-owned locations, and optional canonical backend configuration as consuming-project configuration.

The pre-approval proposal-revalidation design contract requires a deterministic read-only applicability check immediately before approval creation and defines APPLICABLE, STALE, BLOCKED, and INVALID as its primary classifications.

The workflow tests verify immutable definition identity binds intent/authentication, auto-advance requires explicit prospective confirmation, extension events do not advance the normative head, and competing normative transitions fail stale-head checks.

The RIL architecture synthesis defines lifecycle readiness as multiple orthogonal dimensions and requires status classification to surface the highest-precedence blocker rather than hide a materially distinct blocking state.

The operator-management contract prohibits ordinary operator mutations from disabling, demoting, removing, or otherwise mutating the protected root and defines root transfer as a separate current-root-approved ceremony.
The RIL mutation runtime implements canonical JSON serialization and content digests as shared primitives for proposals, approvals, mutation events, projection state, and operation results.
Rupi checkpoint completion is derived from exact primitive result statuses and final Human control return is routed through the accepted human-agent control-return primitive.

The production invocation contract grants the Distiller neither semantic-reconciliation nor admission authority and restricts its semantic project writes to the configured raw candidate artifact and valid candidate submission.

The operational-provenance design contract states that provenance cannot grant or substitute for authentication, approval, Steward authorization or activation, reconciliation judgment, admission authority, or workflow-control authority.
The self-consumption isolation trial reports zero executable source-tree fallback/reference violations and no canonical mutation during the measured installed-runtime invocation.
The authority-grant tests verify approval limits are consumed at issuance, revocation blocks future issuance without invalidating past approval, and issuance/revocation use exact-head concurrency.

The package-builder tests verify two clean builds are byte-identical, only allowlisted roots enter the manifest, project-owned material cannot enter the package, and symlinks inside managed roots fail closed.
The RGP fixture corpus rejects the removed proposition-level authority field.
The package-build configuration ignores generated Python cache artifacts and applies a deterministic default file-mode policy.
The production-invocation tests verify valid fixed evidence produces an immutable candidate submission while exact raw candidate bytes are preserved without post-hoc repair.

The production invocation contract requires raw candidate bytes to be preserved unchanged and prohibits post-model semantic repair, normalization, proposition insertion, kind changes, or provenance rewriting.

The RIL architecture synthesis makes append-only authoritative histories the source of truth for projected administrative and authority state, and states that a projection creates no authority independently of that history.
The Phase 6 parity-evidence workflow captures the parity suite output and persists a parity report rather than treating transient CI success as the only evidence.
The RGP fixture corpus includes an invalid derived proposition whose premise reference does not resolve.
The v2 bootstrap runtime requires project identity to contain exactly non-empty id, name, repository, and summary fields and does not derive those values from repository state.
The proposal-review method instructs the Steward stage to preserve disagreements and uncertainty rather than silently erase them while producing the final disposition and implementation-ready plan.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract limits grant-derived approval issuance to an exact proposal covered by the grant.
The admission runtime recognizes exact idempotent retries from immutable admission receipts before stale-base evaluation and rejects conflicting prior admission evidence.
The shared-orchestration runtime advances auto proposals by composing existing grant, workflow, mutation, and validation primitives and normalizing their failures into an orchestration result.

The R16-R18 implementation conformance plan records gates G1 through G10 as completed and identifies `d1573f326a62f81ce725b62e13824d6d31f81aaf` as the stable verified implementation baseline for the accepted R1-R18 behavior.
The RIL status workflow independently runs and compiles the R9 composite-status conformance suite.

The preserved admission proof explicitly records canonical_written false, making it proof of transaction mechanics rather than evidence that the reference transaction mutated the current project Canon.

The Phase 0 baseline includes adversarial cases for authority promotion, unsupported generalization, premise integrity, contradictory runtime evidence, fabricated provenance, and improper uncertainty promotion.

The RGP Submission Protocol defines immutable candidate submission and immutable Steward disposition as a generic handoff and keeps candidate production, semantic reconciliation, admission, and canonical persistence distinct.
The final install-package plan states that package updates do not silently migrate canonical project knowledge and that integrity, compatibility, drift, and recovery failures fail closed.
The RGP fixture corpus rejects the legacy validated_by relation type.

The Phase-1 acceptance threshold requires no hard failures, perfect precision/provenance/authority-safety scores, and at least 15 of 18 total points, with repeated runs required for stability evidence.

The RIL architecture synthesis separates semantic reconciliation from admission: reconciliation may produce a semantic disposition or admission recommendation, while canonical PEMS/COVE mutation requires a separate admission primitive with valid admission authority.
The package-installer workflow runs both deterministic installer pressure tests and journaled recovery pressure tests.
The role runtime represents role-registry changes as proposed, approved, event-applied transitions and provides replay-based role projection rebuilding.
The installer uses a durable project-local transaction journal to recover interrupted installation and update operations and exposes recovery separately from transition planning.
The RGP fixture corpus includes an invalid cyclic premise graph.
The RIL Steward-authorization workflow independently runs and compiles the R7 Steward-authorization conformance suite.

The Reasoning Distiller Designer directive prioritizes explicit contracts, primitive boundaries, state/lifecycle models, failure semantics, and conformance criteria and instructs design work not to infer or exercise project authority.
The accepted installer-runner contract requires managed-file drift, unsafe archive paths, manifest disagreement, and project-owned path mutation attempts to fail closed.
The admission transaction pressure test exercises exact-base guarded reused-record updates and explicit failure cases rather than mutating a live project Canon.
The uncertainty-import validator deterministically replays the additive RGP/1 uncertainty-to-PEMS compatibility profile.

The operational-provenance design contract makes provenance a non-authoritative non-anchor: optional provenance may be replaced or multiplied without becoming a required identity component of normative artifacts, and operational provenance is not Canon.
The v2 admission executor extends the transaction shape with exact guarded updates to reused records and delegates core transaction mechanics to the shared admission implementation.
The RIL operator-registry workflow independently runs and compiles the R4 protected initial-operator conformance suite.

The live-model activation workflow preserves externally supplied live-model bytes before the measured run, prepares an exact installed-runtime activation bundle, finalizes the untouched model output, and verifies the authority/canonical boundary.

The authority-grant tests verify an exact proposal must be wholly contained by grant scope and that partial/unknown effects, workflow mismatch, terminal workflow state, stale D3, and materiality pauses block issuance.
The invocation-result schema distinguishes successful immutable-submission results from explicit failure results under reasoning-distiller-invocation-result/1.

The operator-registry contract states that installation and bootstrap create no operator authority and requires an explicit initial-root ceremony before the first authority-sensitive operation when no operator registry exists.

The accepted install-package contract requires successful installations to persist the exact verified release manifest and an installation record containing release, content, transport, source, installer, and compatibility metadata while keeping operational event metadata outside package content identity.

The Rupi R5 primitive amendment introduces a protected-confirmation binding primitive so exact Human utterance is bound to an exact protected proposal before authority-specific approval, while the binding result itself has no authority effect.

The final install-package plan states that packaging or installing a generic Steward role definition does not grant Steward authority in a consuming project and that executor/installer mechanics do not acquire semantic authority.

The workflow tests verify materiality pauses suspend continuation, acknowledgements bind exact pauses, completion is primitive-proved and terminal, cancellation is requester/root-only, and revisions create successors while sealing predecessors.

The RIL orchestrator design contract identifies `ril` as the public command identity while retaining Reasoning Distiller as the product and protocol identity, and prohibits inventing a normative acronym expansion for `ril`.

The Frozen Extraction Copy workflow checks out the standalone repository and frozen voxel-engine source separately, verifies the frozen source identity, copies exact framework/reference artifacts, generates provenance, and commits extracted bytes.

The admission contract requires immutable activation, plan, and receipt evidence and permits exact retry as NO_CHANGE only when the receipt and canonical PEMS/COVE bytes agree with the originally admitted result.

The human-agent runtime binds conversational utterances to a bounded set of contextual operations and exposes separate adapter functions for proposal presentation, direct approval, workflows, grants, auto continuation, and protected ceremony boundaries.

The install-package final plan requires the package builder to use an explicit generic-framework allowlist instead of packaging the repository wholesale, and excludes project-specific canonical state, authority, activation, and integration material.
The accepted workflow contract records workflow progression through immutable append-only workflow events.
The install-recovery adapter exposes interrupted-install recovery as a bounded primitive and normalizes recovery success or failure into reasoning-distiller-install-recovery-result/1.
The exact-copy manifest records matching source and destination blob identities for copied framework and reference-corpus artifacts.

The legacy Steward-setup tests verify planning is non-mutating, application requires explicit confirmation and explicit scope, replay is idempotent, and a different authorization never overwrites existing state.
The evaluation scoring rubric measures durable recall, precision, relation integrity, provenance, authority/epistemic safety, and compression on 0–3 scales.

The common mutation substrate requires independent apply-time proposal, basis, state, and governing-domain validation for every authority basis and does not require a previously valid grant-derived approval to lose validity merely because its grant was later revoked.

The self-consumption workflow installs an exact accepted release into the repository, prepares/finalizes through the installed runtime, makes adjacent source framework roots unavailable, audits the installed tree, and emits durable trial evidence.
The Project Bootstrap workflow runs the bootstrap conformance suite as an independent CI gate.

The Phase 6 parity report records PASS for framework isolation, frozen reference blob integrity, frozen Steward transaction proof, guarded update pressure cases, the PEMS/2 contract, project package contract, RGP fixture behavior, and uncertainty import.

The Rupi install-primitive tests verify release verification is read-only, transition planning classifies fresh/no-change/update/downgrade/collision/drift conditions, and a stale successful plan never bypasses installer revalidation.

The initial-operator tests verify an empty project requires an initial operator ceremony, planning is deterministic and mutation-free, exact confirmation is required, and application creates exactly one protected root.

The adversarial Rupi tests verify invalid authoritative history surfaces an exceptional-recovery boundary rather than ordinary repair and local release updates remain deterministic with network blocked.

The Knowledge Systems Architect directive assigns generic representation, schema, backend-interface, validation, migration, compatibility, and package-boundary work while excluding project semantic admission and project-authority assignment.

The reconciliation contract writes one immutable candidate-bound disposition from an explicit assessment only after activation validates for `semantic_reconciliation`, and prohibits reconciliation from invoking admission or mutating canonical PEMS/COVE stores.

The status runtime classifies installation, project bootstrap, authority domains, candidate/reconciliation/admission state, and projection health into a single read-only status result with explicit blockers.
The activation tests verify fail-closed behavior for malformed evidence, unknown activation methods, unassigned scopes, unavailable authorized roles, and conflicting authorization projections.
The installation guide places the installed framework under .reasoning-distiller/ while project knowledge, project rules, and project authority remain outside that managed directory.

The autonomous-workflow tests verify a prospectively authorized chain can complete without Human interruption only while its accepted scope remains valid, with materiality, scope expansion, and protected authority causing interruption before the next consequential mutation.
The first-admission runtime constructs a project-seeded PEMS/2 base from explicit project identity rather than an empty canonical graph.

The RGP validator deterministically validates both raw rgp/1 graphs and submission envelopes, including record/relation vocabulary, provenance shape, premise references/cycles, and structural invariants.
The runtime-isolation record states that P5 proves installed runtime and installer operation do not require network access or a live generic source checkout after package retrieval.
The admission tests verify first admission requires explicit project identity and successful first admission writes schema-valid project-seeded PEMS/COVE plus immutable evidence.
The update/recovery Rupi handoff invokes recovery only for a recovery-required state with bounded recovery intent and always performs a fresh transition plan after recovery.
The role-registry tests verify unauthorized operators and conflicting projections fail closed and role changes create no semantic authority or canonical state.

The Project Knowledge Steward directive assigns project-scoped semantic identity, provenance sufficiency, conflict/supersession/lifecycle, guarded-update, and admission-transaction decisions only within authority granted by the consuming project.
The admission runtime requires an rgp-pems2-admission-transaction/2 plan containing an exact expected canonical PEMS SHA-256 plus explicit reuse, update, new-record, and new-relation sets.
The deterministic-builder record describes P2 as an allowlisted reproducible builder whose clean builds must yield the same canonical manifest/content identity and reject excluded or unsafe content.

The Distiller directive requires compact durable engineering propositions from observable evidence rather than hidden reasoning, limits record/relation vocabularies, and requires primary provenance for non-derived observations.

The installation guide states that updating uses the same deterministic installer with a newer exact accepted release, that managed-tree drift fails closed, and that downgrades are rejected by default.
The preserved Phase 0 evaluation baseline is explicitly evaluation-only and states that it creates no canonical project memory and authorizes no admission.
The Rupi authority confirmation path re-plans from current state, binds an exact protected confirmation, and then invokes existing approval/application primitives.
The proposal-review method separates consequential proposal work into independent invention, independent technical review/synthesis, and Steward reconciliation/final planning stages.

The Distiller core implements deterministic reasoning-distiller-invocation/1 request construction, activation-bundle preparation, raw candidate preservation, RGP validation, and immutable candidate submission.
The operator-management runtime separates ordinary operator changes from protected-root transfer planning, approval, validation, and application.

The mutation tests verify consumed approvals cannot authorize later transitions, stale bases fail without mutation, missing projections are rebuildable, conflicting projections fail closed, and corrupted/non-contiguous event chains are detected.
The accepted CLI and Human-to-Agent contracts require apply-time validation independently after approval creation, including after grant-derived approval.
The journaled-recovery record describes P4 recovery as restoration or completion from durable local transaction state so interrupted installation does not leave an indeterminate managed tree.

The reconciliation-evidence protocol defines an immutable evidence package for evaluating a candidate against a specific canonical snapshot and states that the bundle is evidence rather than authority or admission.
The operator-registry runtime provides a protected initial-operator planning, approval, application, replay, and projection-rebuild path.
The RIL mutation runtime persists authoritative mutation events separately from replaceable projections and can rebuild projections by replaying event history.

The preserved deterministic admission proof records an exact base match, PEMS schema validity, graph integrity, identity/kind preservation, exact guarded-update before state, deterministic repeated PEMS/COVE bytes, and structural COVE round-trip.
The runtime-isolation tests verify installed validators, PEMS backend checks, and admission pressure tests run locally with network blocked and continue after retrieval artifacts are removed.

The deterministic-installer record describes P3 as a staged local installer transaction with integrity checks, compatibility checks, managed-drift detection, idempotent repeat behavior, and deterministic update behavior.

The Human-Agent tests verify context-bound affirmations fail closed, proposal presentation exposes the exact immutable reference, and direct approval performs D3 revalidation immediately before approval creation.
The accepted installer-runner contract prohibits rd_install.py from performing network I/O.
The legacy rd_steward_setup runtime requires explicit authority holder and scope inputs and rejects projects whose project.json is not reasoning-distiller-project/1.
The current production-invocation status record reports PASS and records both canonical-mutation authority and semantic-reconciliation authority as false.
The runtime-isolation workflow combines P5 network/source isolation pressure with retained deterministic installer/recovery proof and a production-invocation local-only check.
The Distiller core rejects evidence symlinks, path escapes, digest mismatches, unresolved source-registry entries, duplicate source identifiers, and mismatched evidence/source-registry metadata.
The Distiller core writes raw candidates and submissions immutably, allowing only exact-byte replay rather than overwrite with different content.
The Rupi authority adapter separates preparation from confirmation for protected initial-root and Steward-authorization ceremonies so control returns to the Human before approval/application.
The RIL orchestrator design contract requires approval to bind to the exact proposed mutation by deterministic digest and states that approval artifacts are not reusable authority credentials.
The current clean-source promotion workflow refuses to push when release-source has moved since the promotion checkout.
The installation-record schema separately records installed release identity, installer identity, managed root, installation time, and compatibility under reasoning-distiller-installation/1.

The Rupi lifecycle-agent design contract defines Rupi as an ephemeral lifecycle adapter with no durable agent identity or authority state and requires consequential actions to map to accepted primitives or shared orchestration rather than Rupi-owned semantics.
The production-invocation tests verify independent invocations receive distinct submission identities and submissions are consumable by the RGP submission protocol validator.

The RIL activation tests verify that role activation requires an available role authorized for the exact requested scope, that authorization scopes remain independent, and that activation itself creates no authority.

The grant-operation tests verify bounded delegated role changes and non-root operator disable can issue/apply through grants, while protected-root disable and non-delegable operator operations cannot.

The governed-ingestion tests verify governed_artifact typing must be explicit, filename wording does not infer governed authority, and selecting one locator with conflicting source types fails closed.

The role-registry contract rejects consumer `rd:*` capabilities and consumer-side Architect or RGP Engineer protocol-governance roles, and requires snapshot submissions to declare explicit role-id scope so absence only affects roles inside that scope.

The bounded-authority-grant design contract states that authority is carried by the grant rather than by the agent and requires complete deterministic proposal containment within both an active grant and its bound immutable workflow.

The RIL orchestrator design contract states that the orchestrator has no semantic-reconciliation or admission authority, the Distiller has candidate-production authority only, and role registration does not itself grant authority.
The operator-management tests verify ordinary authorized managers may add, disable, re-enable, and capability-update non-root operators but cannot change the protected root.
The accepted Human-to-Agent contract binds an authority grant to one immutable workflow.

The final CLI topology tests verify inventories are type-specific, content-artifact inspection cannot invent deeper semantics, aggregate history refuses a fabricated global chronology, and universal apply routes role mutations through the grant-aware boundary.
The current clean-source promotion workflow mirrors default-branch source into release-source while excluding the installed .reasoning-distiller/ tree.
The ordinary-repair runtime validates authoritative history and replaces derived projections without editing the underlying event history.
The runtime-isolation auditor scans an installed Reasoning Distiller tree for executable references that would violate the packaged-runtime isolation boundary.

The admission contract makes R13 the only RIL primitive in its slice allowed to mutate canonical PEMS/COVE and requires a compatible recommended disposition, exact candidate identity, independent admission-scope activation, an exact transaction plan, current-base hash match, and deterministic COVE round-trip.
The workflow runtime implements materiality pause and acknowledgement, cancellation, revision/supersession, completion, and continuation-policy checks as separate event operations.

The greenfield-consumer workflow creates a true greenfield repository, retrieves an exact release read-only, installs and bootstraps using released/installed assets, verifies ownership and authority boundaries, and uploads durable evidence.
The shared-orchestration tests verify non-delegable proposals and absence of applicable grants return an approval boundary rather than manufacturing authority.

The accepted installer-runner contract restricts installer mutation to the declared managed root and transaction/recovery material; project knowledge, canonical state, authority, policy, evidence, adapters, integration, and role activation are not installer-owned.
The CLI tests verify bounded presentation depth, exclusive presentation modes, project override behavior, direct approval routing, and shared workflow-continuation routing.

The bounded-authority-grant design contract prohibits subdelegation and keeps protected-root operations, exceptional recovery authority, grant creation or expansion, workflow-scope revision, and other designated protected operations outside grant delegation.
The greenfield consumer execution record reports that the original v0.2.0 trial stopped because public bootstrap was undefined, producing finding GFCT-001 rather than inventing project scaffolding.

The operation-delegability classification records `role-registry.change` and exact non-root `operator-registry.disable` as the accepted v1 grant-delegable operation classes, while Steward authorization changes, exceptional recovery, authority-grant creation or expansion, workflow revision, and materiality acknowledgement remain non-delegable.
The project-v2 compatibility tests verify Distiller ingestion accepts validated reasoning-distiller-project/2 configuration, retains exact v1 compatibility, and rejects invalid v2 identity.

The Rupi end-to-end tests exercise fresh project setup, independently bound protected authority mutations, verified updates preserving project-owned state, conversation-free resume from durable state, and configured-project readiness without fake mutation.
The accepted installer-runner contract requires rd_install.py to consume local files and an explicit project target.
The accepted RIL CLI contract defines the CLI as an adapter over shared Reasoning Distiller primitives and orchestration rather than a new semantic or authority layer.

The greenfield first-invocation specification requires installed prepare/finalize to operate on explicit project-owned evidence, preserve provider-boundary raw bytes exactly, create an immutable valid candidate submission, and stop without reconciliation or admission state.
The Phase 6 parity report records 15 Phase-1 raw candidates and 5 Phase-3 shadow candidates as unchanged under parity validation.

The Steward-authorization tests verify unknown/unavailable targets and unauthorized operators are rejected, approval is bound to the exact proposal, projection conflicts fail closed, and authorization creates no semantic or canonical state.
The RGP fixture corpus includes an invalid non-derived observation without primary provenance.
The mutation tests verify canonical JSON/digest determinism, proposal creation without filesystem mutation, approval binding to exact proposals, append/replay behavior, and idempotent retries.
